name: Podkidnoy Durak (Durak Podkidnoy)
description: Podkidnoy Durak (historically translated as 'Throw-in Fool') is the most popular and strategically intense variant of the traditional Russian game Durak. Unlike the basic variant where an attack consists of a single card, Podkidnoy allows all other players to 'Throw In' cards that match the rank of any attacking or defending card on the table. It is a game of shifting alliances, brutal resource management, and the unique goal of simply NOT being the loser.

history.origins: Durak emerged in the late 18th century as a 'Commoners' game' in imperial Russia. The 'Podkidnoy' variant was popularized in the Soviet era, becoming the definitive version played in schools, trains, and at home.
timeline: 1800s: Durak replaces Piquet and Pharaon as the most-played card game among Russian peasants.
1920s: Rules for 'Throwing In' are standardized across the USSR.
1990s: Reaches a global audience via early internet card game servers.
Present: Remains a core part of Russian culture, with professional tournaments and millions of online players.
history.cultural: In Russia, being the 'Durak' (the fool) is seen as a playful dishonor, often resulting in the loser having to fetch tea or deal the next 10 hands.
history.evolution: The Podkidnoy mechanic was introduced to prevent players from simply 'Sitting on trumps'â€”it forces active engagement in every round of defense.

setup.dealing: Each player receives 6 cards. The next card is placed face-up under the deck to set TRUMP. This card is the last one to be drawn.

rules.objective: Be the first to shed all cards. The last player with cards is the 'Durak'.
rules.gameplay: Attack; defender beats or picks up. Others may add same-rank cards. Refill from stock. Last with cards loses.
keyRules: Players must follow legal action constraints on every turn.
Round resolution and scoring follow the documented win rules.

strategy.basic: Pick up early to win later! If you are the Defender and the attack is 'Small' (Low numbers), it's often better to intentionally pick up those cards. This fills your hand with cards that allow you to defend better later, and it 'Starves' the attackers of the chance to throw in their high-value trumps. In Durak, a large hand of low cards is sometimes better than a small hand of high cards because of the throw-in mechanic.
strategy.intermediate: The 'Podkidnoy' Trap: As an Attacker, don't throw in your cards immediately. Wait for the Defender to play a trump. If they play a Trump 9, and you have a Heart 9 in your hand, throw it in. You are forcing them to waste a SECOND trump to beat it. Exhausting the Defender's trumps is the fastest way to make them pick up.
strategy.advanced: Card Counting (The Trump Count): Since there are only 9 cards per suit, and you know the dealer's trump card at the bottom, you can calculate almost exactly how many trumps are in play. In the late-game (when the deck is empty), if you know the Defender doesn't have the Ace of Trump, you can lead your King with absolute confidence. Focus on saving at least one high trump for the final '1-on-1' showdown.
tips: If playing in teams, never throw in cards that match the rank of your PARTNER'S lead unless it's to force a pick-up.
The first player to shed all their cards is safeâ€”they don't care who becomes the Durak.

variations.name: Duraka uchat / Is pod duraka
variations.description: Who attacks first after the fool deals: Duraka uchat (fool is taught) means the player to the right of the dealer attacks first; Is pod duraka (we go from under the fool) means the player to the left of the dealer attacks first.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Rule affects turn order only; no engine constant overrides needed for this variant.

variations.name: Trump 6 exchange
variations.description: Some players do not allow the trump 6 to be exchanged for the face-up trump; some allow exchange for the ace only.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Optional rule; engine can support both via option; no numeric overrides.

variations.name: 52-card pack for 5-6 players
variations.description: When five or six play, a full 52-card pack may be used; the two of trumps (instead of the six) can then be exchanged for the face-up trump. Rare variation.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Different deck size and exchange card; would require separate game config.
